transcript: This past weekend, my boyfriend Paul and I saw Shadow Land at the public, a new play described as a lyrical meditation on legacy, erotic fugitivity, and self determination. In the play, a woman named Ruth and her elderly mother are trapped in the bar their family owns as Hurricane Katrina is taking her toll in and around New Orleans. Ruth is also working through a sense of claustrophobia in her own life, feeling that she hasn't made something of herself beyond the cards and circumstances she's been given. As she and her mother debate and share their perspectives with one another, the scenes between them is interspersed with 1/3 character. This character voices, often directly to the audience, what I would describe as poetic commentary that reflects the other character's experiences and brings up the effects of disaster, displacement, and the devastating in action that often follows. This play was so well thought out and sheds light on something really important in a uniquely theatrical way. Shadowland is running to the anime, so definitely go see it with that another playbook for my collection.
